subtitle: Settings, habits and extensions for any browser.

subsections.title: Safer Browsing Habits
subsections.summary: Settings and habits for any browser.

items.details: Most updates fix security holes. Firefox and Chrome update themselves, but check now and then; Tor Browser updates separately.
One hardened browser for sensitive things (banking, health, activism), another for everyday browsing.

items.text: Set a private default search engine
items.details: DuckDuckGo, Brave Search, Mojeek or Startpage. See search engines.

items.text: Type addresses instead of searching for them
items.details: Searching a bank’s name can surface lookalike scam sites. Turn off search suggestions in the address bar.
Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → HTTPS-Only Mode. Chrome: “Always use secure connections”.
Firefox: Enhanced Tracking Protection on Strict (drop to Standard if sites break). Chrome: block third-party cookies and use Enhanced Safe Browsing.

items.text: Review camera, microphone and location permissions
items.details: Only allow them for sites you trust, and remove old permissions.

items.text: Don’t save passwords in the browser
items.details: Use a password manager instead, and delete the logins your browser saved.
Install only from the official add-on stores and remove anything you don’t use or recognise — every extension can see your browsing.
Set the browser to clear cookies and site data when it closes, and don’t reopen the last session on startup.
They can send the page you’re reading to the browser maker. Firefox: Settings → AI Controls. Chrome: turn off Gemini features.
If the browser warns a site is dangerous, don’t continue. Pause before opening links sent by message or email.

items.label: uBlock Origin
items.desc: The essential ad and tracker blocker. Full version works in Firefox.

items.label: uBlock Origin Lite
items.desc: The version for Chrome, Edge, Brave and Safari.

items.label: ClearURLs
items.desc: Strips tracking codes out of the links you click.

items.label: Decentraleyes
items.desc: Serves common web libraries locally so third parties don’t see the request.

items.label: Cookie AutoDelete
items.desc: Deletes a site’s cookies when you close its tab.

items.label: SponsorBlock
items.desc: Skips sponsor segments in YouTube videos.

items.label: Privacy Badger
items.desc: EFF’s tracker blocker that learns as you browse.

items.label: NoScript
items.desc: Blocks scripts on sites you don’t trust. Advanced — breaks many sites.

blocks.before: Start with an ad blocker — uBlock Origin on Firefox, uBlock Origin Lite on Chrome-based browsers and Safari. Add others only if you need them. See Browser Extensions for setup.

blocks.html: Safari: uBlock Origin Lite and SponsorBlock are available from the App Store; AdGuard (a sponsored pick on privacytools.io) is another option.
